item.title: Missed your exit: can you reverse on the hard shoulder?
item.description: You must not reverse on a motorway. This includes the hard shoulder. Missing your exit does not create an exception to the rule.

item.title: Red light on a priority road: must you stop?
item.description: You must stop at red even on a priority road. Traffic lights take precedence over signs controlling priority. A B1 sign does not allow you to drive through red.

item.title: Can you use your rear fog light in heavy rain?
item.description: Rain alone does not allow you to use your rear fog light, even with visibility of 40 metres. You may use it in fog or snow when visibility is less than 50 metres.

item.title: Cyclist coming from the right: who has priority?
item.description: At a junction with paved roads and no signs, traffic lights or give-way triangles, give way to drivers and riders from the right. That includes cyclists.

item.title: Minimum car tyre tread depth: how many millimetres?
item.description: A car tyre must have at least 1.6 mm of tread in its main grooves around the entire circumference of the tread. Wear indicators are excluded from the measurement.

item.title: Does waiting in your car count as parking?
item.description: Waiting for someone who is still indoors and is not getting in immediately counts as parking. Staying in the car does not change that.

item.title: Can you hold your phone for navigation while driving?
item.description: You must not hold a mobile electronic device while driving, even to check directions. The rule applies whether you are making a call, reading a message or checking a map.

item.title: Turning right: does the cyclist beside you go first?
item.description: If you are travelling on the same road, let the cyclist go first. You are turning while the cyclist continues straight ahead. Using your indicator does not change the order.

item.title: Can you pass on the right in queuing traffic?
item.description: In queuing traffic, you may pass a queue on the right. You do not have to stay behind the car to your left when your lane is moving faster.

item.title: How to round up the time on a blue parking disc
item.description: You may round your arrival time up to the next hour or half-hour. If you arrive at 10:10, that means 10:30. You cannot choose any later time you like.

item.title: Amber traffic lights: should you stop or keep going?
item.description: Amber means stop. You may continue only if you can no longer reasonably stop safely. If you can stop safely before the stop line, you must do so.

item.title: When should you dip your headlights for a cyclist?
item.description: You must not use full beam when meeting another road user. A cyclist is a road user too, so switch to dipped headlights.

item.title: Leaving a driveway: do pedestrians go first?
item.description: When leaving a driveway, let all other traffic go first. That includes a runner on the pavement.
